cases.answer_before_fail_closed: DPR with FAISS has a significantly faster runtime compared to BM25 using Lucene. DPR achieves a processing speed of 995.0 questions per second, returning top 100 passages per question, whereas BM25/Lucene processes only 23.7 questions per second per CPU thread [2]. However, the time required to build an FAISS index for dense vectors is longer than that for an inverted index using Lucene, taking approximately 8.8 hours on 8 GPUs, whereas building an inverted index using Lucene takes only about 30 minutes [4].

expected_claims: Larger chunks can preserve more context but introduce more noise, processing time, and cost.
Smaller chunks contain less noise but may fail to preserve all necessary context.
Small2Big retrieves small units and supplies surrounding sentences as larger context to the language model.

cases.answer: The choice of chunk size in a RAG system involves balancing semantic completeness and context length [5]. Larger chunks capture more context but introduce more noise, increasing processing time and costs [5]. Conversely, smaller chunks provide less noise but may not fully convey necessary context [5]. Methods like recursive splits and sliding windows aim to merge globally related information across multiple retrieval processes, yet still struggle to find an optimal balance [5].
